name: Match an object to its net
description: Student can match a three-dimensional object to its two-dimensional net.
exampleOfSuccess: The student matches a cube to the net with six squares.
commonError: Student matches by the number of pieces without checking they fold up.
checkpointTask: Show objects and nets. Ask the student to match each object to its net.

name: Identify the faces in a net
description: Student can identify how the faces of a net relate to the object.
exampleOfSuccess: The student points out which square of a cube net becomes the top.
commonError: Student cannot track which face goes where when folded.
checkpointTask: Show a net. Ask the student to identify the faces of the folded object.

name: Build an object from its net
description: Student can build a three-dimensional object from its net.
exampleOfSuccess: The student folds a net to build a triangular prism.
commonError: Student folds a net that does not close up into the object.
checkpointTask: Give a net. Ask the student to build the object.

name: Sketch a net for an object
description: Student can sketch a net for a given prism or pyramid.
exampleOfSuccess: The student sketches a correct net for a square pyramid.
commonError: Student sketches a net with the wrong number or arrangement of faces.
checkpointTask: Name a prism or pyramid. Ask the student to sketch a net for it.

name: Plot a point with coordinates
description: Student can plot a point on a grid using coordinates.
exampleOfSuccess: The student plots (3, 2) by going across 3 and up 2.
checkpointTask: Give coordinates and a grid. Ask the student to plot each point.

name: Read the coordinates of a point
description: Student can read the coordinates of a point on a grid.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads a point as (4, 1).
commonError: Student gives the coordinates in the wrong order.
checkpointTask: Mark points on a grid. Ask the student to give the coordinates of each.

name: Describe movement using coordinates
description: Student can describe movement between points using coordinates and directional language.
exampleOfSuccess: The student describes moving from (1, 1) to (1, 4) as up 3.
commonError: Student describes a move that does not match the coordinates.
checkpointTask: Give two points. Ask the student to describe the movement between them.

name: Construct a coordinate system
description: Student can construct a grid coordinate system and use it to locate positions.
exampleOfSuccess: The student draws labelled axes and plots given positions correctly.
commonError: Student labels the axes inconsistently so points cannot be located.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to set up a coordinate grid and plot given positions.

name: Perform a translation
description: Student can translate a shape and describe the movement.
exampleOfSuccess: The student slides a shape 3 right and 2 down and describes it.
commonError: Student rotates or reflects the shape instead of translating.
checkpointTask: Give a shape. Ask the student to translate it and describe the move.

name: Perform a reflection
description: Student can reflect a shape across a line.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reflects a shape across a vertical line so it mirrors.
commonError: Student translates the shape instead of mirroring it.
checkpointTask: Give a shape and a mirror line. Ask the student to reflect it.

name: Perform a rotation
description: Student can rotate a shape about a point.
exampleOfSuccess: The student rotates a shape a quarter turn about a corner.
commonError: Student moves the shape without turning it.
checkpointTask: Give a shape and a centre. Ask the student to rotate it a given turn.

name: Describe what stays the same
description: Student can describe what changes and what stays the same under a transformation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the shape's size stays the same but its position changes.
commonError: Student thinks the shape changes size or form under a slide or turn.
checkpointTask: After a transformation, ask the student what changed and what stayed the same.

name: Identify symmetry in a pattern
description: Student can identify the symmetries in a transformed pattern.
exampleOfSuccess: The student identifies a line of symmetry in a reflected pattern.
commonError: Student confuses the types of symmetry, or misses one.
checkpointTask: Show a transformed pattern. Ask the student to identify its symmetries.
